binders: Universally quantified types ι and Ω, where ι is finite and Ω is measurable.
A probability measure μ on Ω.
A finite indexed family X : ι → Ω → Real.
A proof that the index type is nonempty.
Universally quantified real parameters λ and t.
hypotheses: Every X_i is integrable with respect to μ and has integral zero.
For every i, LocalDef001 μ (X_i) is strictly below ENNReal infinity.
The indexed family X is jointly independent with respect to μ.
conclusions: The ENNReal measure of the one-sided event {ω : Σ_i X_i(ω) ≥ t} is at most ofReal(exp(-λt)) multiplied by the finite product over i of ∫⁻_Ω ofReal(exp(λX_i(ω))) dμ(ω).
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 μ X is the ENNReal infimum of all LocalDef002-admissible scales.
LocalDef002 μ X s means that X is measurable, s is neither zero nor infinity, exp(|X|/s.toReal) is μ-integrable, and its μ-integral is at most 2.
The random sum is the unweighted finite sum S(ω) = Σ_i X_i(ω).
Each factor in the product is the nonnegative extended-real integral M_i(λ) = ∫⁻_Ω ofReal(exp(λX_i(ω))) dμ(ω).
Because real exponentials are positive, ofReal(exp(y)) is the usual ENNReal embedding of exp(y).
The right-hand side is exp(-λt), embedded in ENNReal, times Π_i M_i(λ).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every nonempty finite jointly independent family of measurable, integrable, mean-zero real random variables on a probability space, with each variable having finite LocalDef001 gauge, and for every λ > 0 and t ≥ 0, the probability of the upper-tail event that their sum is at least t is bounded by exp(-λt) times the product of their individual nonnegative extended-real exponential moments at λ.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type must be finite and nonempty; empty families are excluded.
The result is one-sided: it concerns Σ_i X_i ≥ t, not an absolute-value event.
The threshold relation is non-strict, while λ must be strictly positive and t need only be nonnegative.
The conclusion is ENNReal-valued and uses lintegrals, so any individual exponential moment may equal infinity.
If any product factor is infinity, the right-hand side may be infinity and the bound can become vacuous.
Finiteness of LocalDef001, centering, and integrability are explicit antecedents even though LocalDef001 does not otherwise appear in the displayed bound.
All hypotheses are implications' antecedents, so failure of measurability, centering, gauge finiteness, or independence makes the proposition trivially true for that data.
No quantitative upper bound on the individual exponential moments is asserted.
No weighting or normalization is applied to the finite sum.
ambiguities: The dossier defines LocalDef001 exactly but gives it no conventional mathematical name, so it can only be described by its defining infimum.
The lintegrals are allowed to be infinite; the proposition does not state separate finite-MGF hypotheses.
